rationale: Preserve Summit Ridge Energy as an active U.S. distributed-solar platform and preserve Apollo-managed funds as the current legal owner while the announced GIP transaction remains unclosed. Apollo's official 2022 announcement establishes its $175 million platform investment, and Apollo's current Wilson Handler profile continued to call Summit Ridge an Apollo funds portfolio company as of August 12, 2026. Correct the unsupported Apollo vehicle and stake fields to not-publicly-disclosed values. Record the July 14, 2026 agreement by Global Infrastructure Partners, a part of BlackRock, to acquire a majority and controlling interest through GIP's mid-market strategy as a signed pending exit linked to Apollo's active ownership period. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals; no legal-closing announcement was found through August 12, 2026, so GIP is not an active owner and Apollo is not retired. The official transaction announcement does not disclose the exact stake, consideration, specific GIP fund, seller allocation or Apollo's possible residual interest. Apollo's separate April 2025 commitment relates to an Illinois solar-asset joint venture and is not a second corporate ownership period. Sixth Street's association is debt-only and remains excluded. A related Deal Database record already exists but stores July 17 rather than the primary July 14 announcement date; that discrepancy is documented for separate deal review and is not mutated here.

beforeImage.name: Summit Ridge Energy
beforeImage.description: Summit Ridge Energy develops, owns, and operates distributed generation and community solar assets in the United States. Its customers include commercial offtakers, community solar subscribers, utilities, and other power purchasers, and the business follows an asset-heavy, contracted model with development, financing, and long-term operating capabilities. Company materials state that Summit Ridge has more than 2 GW of solar projects operating or in development, has financed more than 200 facilities, and has raised over $5 billion of project capital since launch. The platform operates nationally, with public disclosures around Apollo's 2025 investment highlighting Illinois commercial solar assets. Apollo announced in April 2025 that its funds had committed up to $400 million to a new commercial solar partnership with Summit Ridge, while public sources do not disclose the broader platform-level ownership percentages.

afterImage.name: Summit Ridge Energy
afterImage.description: Summit Ridge Energy develops, constructs, owns, and operates distributed solar and battery-storage systems across the U.S. Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, and New England. Founded in 2017, the company reported more than 275 facilities and over 3 GW of operating and development-stage solar and storage projects in July 2026. Apollo-managed funds made a $175 million strategic platform investment in 2022; the exact Apollo stake, fund and legal vehicle are not publicly disclosed. On July 14, 2026, Global Infrastructure Partners, a part of BlackRock, agreed through its mid-market infrastructure strategy to acquire a majority and controlling interest, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. No closing announcement was identified through August 12, 2026, so Apollo remains the current legal owner and GIP is recorded only as a signed pending counterparty. Apollo's separate 2025 commitment of up to $400 million relates to an Illinois solar-asset joint venture rather than a second corporate ownership period.
